comments.text:
Proprietary memory cards, developing for the vita was expensive to say the least early on, not many games, 3G not delivering as advertised (which they got hit with a class action)... And the crazy part is that the Vita fails harder than the PSP Go even in hindsight. And failed where the PSP Go already had the issue solved.

The Go was a product WAY ahead of its time conceptually. A digital console in an era not ready for it. But the cool thing about it is that it has 16GB of onboard storage where the Vita had under 1GB. For a handheld advertised as having console level quality, they sure wanted to recoup money by having people buy storage. But also, instead of licensing the creation of the card to manufacturers, they decided to shoulder the burden of making cards unlike the PSP Cards. Another thing about their storage is that it was only for the Vita. The Memory Stick Pro and the PSP Go sticks are also could be used as storage for the Sony cameras and camcorders at the time.

The Go was a product WAY ahead of its time conceptually. A digital console in an era not ready for it. But the cool thing about it is that it has 16GB of onboard storage where the Vita had under 1GB. For a handheld advertised as having console level quality, they sure wanted to recoup money by having people buy storage. But also, instead of licensing the creation of the card to manufacturers, they decided to shoulder the burden of making cards unlike the PSP Cards. Another thing about their storage is that it was only for the Vita. The Memory Stick Pro and the PSP Go sticks are also could be used as storage for the Sony cameras and camcorders at the time.
